# @codenhub/icons

## Functions

### adoptIconifySet

```ts
export declare function adoptIconifySet(source: IconifyJson, options?: IconifyAdapterOptions): IconFamilyData;
```

Adopts an IconifyJSON-shaped icon set as a family this registry can resolve.

Icon bodies are taken as authored; only the metadata this package requires and Iconify does not carry — obligation level, tier, provenance — is filled in. Adopted sets are always `"extended"` tier: the package makes its licensing promise about the families it generates, not about data a consumer supplies.

**Parameters**

- `source` — IconifyJSON document, such as the default export of an `@iconify-json` package.
- `options` — Obligation level and stroke behavior the document cannot state.

**Returns** — Family data ready for `IconRegistry.registerFamily`.

### generateBaseCss

```ts
export declare function generateBaseCss(options?: BaseCssOptions): string;
```

Generates the base rules every icon class builds on.

An icon is an element that carries an icon class: an `<i>` (or `.${p}` on any element you own) rendered as a mask, or an inlined `<svg>` sized and coloured from the same custom properties. There is no `::before`, `::after`, or form-control form — an icon beside a label is a real `<i>` inside the control — so the base rules are just those two element forms plus the `${p}-xs`–`${p}-xl` size axis.

The size axis is five one-line rules that each set `--${p}-size` to a rem value. Both forms above already read `var(--${p}-size, 1em)`, so a size class needs no knowledge of the element it lands on and the unclassed default stays `1em`. The classes are always emitted because they cost almost nothing and a scanner cannot know a project is about to use one. `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, and `xl` are reserved names for this reason — no family may ship an icon or take a prefix by one.

An icon paints in `--${p}-color` when one is set on it or an ancestor, else in its own artwork when it is multicolor (which its icon rule sets as `--${p}-brand-paint`), else in its own color when it has one (a brand mark's, set as `--${p}-brand-color`), else in `currentColor`. The `background` shorthand carries all four, because the artwork is an image and the rest are colors.

**Parameters**

- `options` — Class prefix.

**Returns** — The base stylesheet.

### generateFamilyCss

```ts
export declare function generateFamilyCss(family: IconFamilyData, options?: GenerateFamilyCssOptions): string;
```

Generates the complete stylesheet for one icon family.

Every icon is written out, because this is the plugin-free path: nothing is scanning the consumer's markup, so nothing can narrow the family down. A project chooses its cost one family at a time, by choosing which families it imports.

Stroke width cannot be varied here. It is baked into the artwork each rule carries, and a stylesheet with no build step behind it has no way to know which widths a project wants, so `ic-heart/1.5` needs one of the plugins.

**Parameters**

- `family` — Family to write out.
- `options` — Class prefix, bare name selectors, and the license notice.

**Returns** — The family stylesheet.

### generateIconSetCss

```ts
export declare function generateIconSetCss(classes: Iterable<string>, registry: IconRegistry, options?: GenerateIconSetCssOptions): IconSetCssResult;
```

Generates the stylesheet for a set of scanned icon classes.

Icons sharing identical markup are grouped into one rule, so a class and its aliases cost a selector rather than a second copy of the artwork. Classes that resolve to no icon are skipped silently, because a scanner reports every prefixed class it sees, including ones that are not icons.

A class carrying a stroke modifier, as in `ic-heart/1.5`, renders at that width. One class is one rule: the width is part of the artwork the rule carries, so only the widths the markup actually asked for are generated.

**Parameters**

- `classes` — Scanned class names, stroke modifiers included.
- `registry` — Registry holding the loaded families.
- `options` — Class prefix, base rule injection, and default stroke width.

**Returns** — The stylesheet and the families it drew from.

### renderSvg

```ts
export declare function renderSvg(icon: ResolvedIcon, options?: RenderSvgOptions): string;
```

Renders a resolved icon as a complete, self-contained SVG element.

The element carries a namespace, a viewBox, a `1em` box, and `fill="currentColor"`, leaving color to CSS. The fill is for bodies that set none of their own, such as Material Symbols and Simple Icons paths, which SVG would otherwise paint black whatever `color` says; a body that sets its own fill, as Lucide's `fill="none"` does, still wins. The `1em` box is a floor for an icon inlined with no stylesheet behind it, which a bare `viewBox` renders at 0×0. It is a presentation attribute, so CSS `width`/`height` still wins — including the base stylesheet's `svg[class^="ic-"]` rule, which reads `--ic-size` and `--ic-color` and so carries the `ic-xs`–`ic-xl` size axis and the colour custom property onto an inlined icon the same as onto an `<i>`. Passing `width`, `height`, or `fill` in `RenderSvgOptions.attributes` replaces the default. The viewBox keeps the icon's own origin, because families such as Material Symbols draw above it. A stroke width is applied only when the icon's family is stroke-based.

An icon with a color of its own, such as a brand mark, is painted in it unless `--ic-color` is set on the element or an ancestor. The color sits on a `<g>` around the body rather than on the `<svg>`, so it never collides with a `style` attribute a caller or the markup puts on the element. The `<g>` also carries the color as a presentation attribute: a Content Security Policy that blocks style attributes drops the `style`, and the icon keeps its own color, though `--ic-color` no longer reaches it.

A multicolor icon keeps the colors its artwork is drawn in, and `--ic-color` repaints every fill and stroke as a one-color silhouette. Each painted element carries its own `style` declaration for this, beside the attribute it falls back to, so the same Content Security Policy leaves the logo in full color.

**Parameters**

- `icon` — Icon to render.
- `options` — Stroke width, extra element attributes, and class prefix.

**Returns** — SVG markup.

### resolveIconClassName

```ts
export declare function resolveIconClassName(registry: IconRegistry, name: string): ResolvedIcon | undefined;
```

Resolves the icon part of a utility class, where a family prefix is written with a dash because a class name cannot contain a colon.

`x` resolves through the default prefix, while `lucide-heart` resolves to `lucide:heart`. The longest matching family prefix wins, so a family named `material-symbols-outlined` is preferred over one named `material` when both are loaded.

**Parameters**

- `registry` — Registry holding the loaded families.
- `name` — Icon part of the class, with the utility prefix already stripped.

**Returns** — The resolved icon, or `undefined` when no reading of the name resolves.

## Classes

### IconRegistry

```ts
export declare class IconRegistry
```

Holds icon families and resolves icon names against them.

Families are registered either as loaded data or as loaders invoked the first time one of their icons is requested. Build-time consumers stay on the synchronous `IconRegistry.resolve`, because a build knows which families it needs before it starts; runtime consumers use `IconRegistry.resolveAsync`, which loads a family on demand.

#### constructor

```ts
constructor(options?: IconRegistryOptions);
```

Creates a registry holding no families.

**Parameters**

- `options` — Default prefix for unqualified names.

#### getFamily

```ts
getFamily(prefix: string): IconFamilyData | undefined;
```

Returns loaded family data by prefix.

Consumers use it to read family metadata such as license and attribution.

**Parameters**

- `prefix` — Family prefix to read.

#### has

```ts
has(name: string): boolean;
```

Reports whether an icon name resolves against the families already loaded.

**Parameters**

- `name` — Icon name, qualified or not.

#### list

```ts
list(prefix?: string): string[];
```

Lists the primary icon names of a loaded family, excluding aliases.

**Parameters**

- `prefix` — Family prefix to list. Defaults to the configured default prefix.

#### listFamilies

```ts
listFamilies(): string[];
```

Lists the prefixes of every family currently loaded.

#### load

```ts
load(prefix: string): Promise<IconFamilyData>;
```

Loads a registered family so it becomes available to synchronous resolution.

Concurrent calls for the same prefix share one load. An already-loaded family is returned as-is without invoking its loader again.

**Parameters**

- `prefix` — Family prefix to load.

#### registerFamily

```ts
registerFamily(family: IconFamilyData): void;
```

Registers already-loaded family data under its own prefix.

Registering a prefix that already holds a family replaces it, which is what lets a project override a bundled family with its own artwork.

**Parameters**

- `family` — Family data to make resolvable.

#### registerLoader

```ts
registerLoader(prefix: string, loader: IconFamilyLoader): void;
```

Registers a loader invoked the first time an icon of this prefix is requested asynchronously.

The family stays absent from synchronous resolution until it is loaded, so a build-time consumer must await `IconRegistry.load` first.

**Parameters**

- `prefix` — Family prefix the loader provides.
- `loader` — Function returning the family data, typically a dynamic import.

#### resolve

```ts
resolve(name: string): ResolvedIcon | undefined;
```

Resolves an icon name against the families already loaded.

An unqualified name resolves against the configured default prefix, and against nothing at all when none is set. A name whose family is registered only as a loader does not resolve here.

**Parameters**

- `name` — Icon name, qualified (`"lucide:x"`) or not (`"x"`).

#### resolveAsync

```ts
resolveAsync(name: string): Promise<ResolvedIcon | undefined>;
```

Resolves an icon name, loading its family first when it is not yet available.

**Parameters**

- `name` — Icon name, qualified (`"lucide:x"`) or not (`"x"`).

## Type aliases

### AttributionMode

```ts
export type AttributionMode = "auto" | "file" | "off";
```

How a build emits the license notices of the families it used.

### IconAttribution

```ts
export type IconAttribution = "none" | "notice" | "credit";
```

Obligation a family's license places on the consumer who ships its icons.

- `"none"`: public-domain dedications such as CC0 and Unlicense. Nothing is owed in distributed output.
- `"notice"`: permissive licenses such as MIT, ISC, and Apache-2.0. The copyright and license notice must be preserved in distributions, which the build integrations emit automatically.
- `"credit"`: licenses such as CC-BY that require crediting the author visibly, beyond preserving a notice.

### IconFamilyLoader

```ts
export type IconFamilyLoader = () => Promise<IconFamilyData | {
    default: IconFamilyData;
}>;
```

Loads a family's data the first time one of its icons is requested.

Returning the module namespace of a dynamic import is supported directly, so `() => import("@codenhub/icons/data/lucide")` is a valid loader.

### IconFamilyTier

```ts
export type IconFamilyTier = "core" | "extended" | "brand";
```

Catalog tier a family belongs to.

`"core"` families are public-domain or notice-only, and their obligations are satisfied by the notice the build emits. `"extended"` families are opt-in and outside the package's licensing promise: their `info.attribution` says whether a notice or author credit is owed. A generated extended family owes credit; a set adopted through `adoptIconifySet` is always extended, and owes whatever its caller declared. `"brand"` families hold logos and brand marks: they owe nothing on the copyright side, are opt-in, and remain subject to each brand owner's trademark guidelines, which no build setting satisfies.
